title: Gimmer refuge
description: Build a small refuge halfway up a cliff.
image_alt: A timber refuge under construction on a narrow mountain ledge, with a pulley raising materials.
predicament: Materials must reach a mountain ledge before a base, walls and roof can come together. Crews, lifting equipment, handovers and decisions about change all affect what can happen next.
motivation: One imagined refuge supports several enquiries: which plans are possible, how work packages combine, what a schedule reveals, and how different accounts of the project connect.
limitation: These enquiries share a setting. Each uses its own assumptions and rules; their results are not a single engineered refuge plan.

title: The farm track
description: Deliver concrete while the farm carries on.
image_alt: A concrete mixer waits at a farm gate while cows occupy the narrow lane to a foundation pour.
predicament: The site needs concrete. The farmer needs to take cattle to market. Both plans depend on the same narrow lane, so work that makes sense on its own may have to wait.
motivation: Follow the shared access through one process model, then ask what changes when the project and its surroundings are viewed together.
limitation: Cattle passage is a selected toy scenario, not a probability forecast. The model makes the resource conflict explicit.

projects.description: Try the lane and inspect why one process must wait for another.

title: A wildlife crossing
description: Reconnect two habitats across a busy road.
image_alt: Deer on a green bridge, with guiding fences, a monitoring camera and a power cabinet.
predicament: A bridge alone does not reconnect the habitats. Guiding fences, observation, construction access and monitoring power must also fit the promised crossing.
motivation: Explore the finished configuration, the stages that deliver it, programme trade-offs and the work needed to support remote monitoring.
limitation: The four enquiries use separate declared models. They are not numerically coupled into one delivery design.

title: A brick rotunda
description: Build a circular wall, course by course.
image_alt: A circular brick wall under construction, with stacked bricks and lifting equipment.
predicament: Two walls with the same amount of finished work may have different readiness, histories or available lifting capacity. Those differences can change the next useful move.
motivation: Begin with choices and histories, then examine a finite construction in which two brick rings share hoists and obey explicit placement and curing rules.
limitation: The simple primer and the later construction have different rules. Their results concern those toy rules, not a building forecast.

title: The Tangled Triangle
description: Fit a control centre onto an awkward site.
image_alt: A control-centre site squeezed between a canal, road and railway viaduct.
predicament: A fictional control-centre site must contend with a canal, road, railway viaduct, overhead power line and old mine passage. Plans, sections and local constraints reveal different parts of the problem.
motivation: The same site supports two enquiries: how AI interprets a brief, and whether declared local rules admit a shared candidate location.
limitation: The interpretation variants are not a scored AI benchmark. The compatibility lab checks sampled locations under supplied rules, not real-site feasibility.

title: Shared waters
description: Connect an offshore depot and a power barge.
image_alt: A power barge moored beside an offshore depot, with a service connection between them.
predicament: An offshore depot needs power. A floating barge could supply it, but the service also depends on access, information, resources and the organisations that provide them.
motivation: Explore what becomes clearer when equipment and organisations expose explicit boundaries, handovers and shared observations.
limitation: This fictional depot and SMR-barge setting motivates three small constructions; it does not establish engineering feasibility or a delivery plan.

title: A wall and its roof
description: Build a wall that is ready for the next trade.
image_alt: A brick wall and partly assembled pitched roof, with scaffold and building materials.
predicament: Brickwork needs materials, workers and access. The roof needs a wall with the right support and readiness. Connecting the packages must preserve those conditions.
motivation: Follow the construction into reusable work blocks, the meanings of their wiring and the repeated work that grows a wall.
limitation: A correctly connected diagram and a satisfied readiness condition are different checks. Each essay states the construction rules it actually tests.

title: A tunnel beneath the Solway
description: Find the work hidden behind a finished tunnel.
image_alt: A cutaway of a tunnel beneath the Solway, with shore access and construction underground.
predicament: A tunnel needs more than its permanent lining. Excavation, temporary access, support, installed systems and evidence of readiness each have a different part to play.
motivation: Use the tunnel setting and smaller installation examples to distinguish the desired result from the work, temporary means and evidence it requires.
limitation: The installation examples test selected distinctions. They do not provide a complete tunnel plan, and the retained Tokyo and HS2 ontology examples are separate cases.

projects.title: From an outcome to its work

title: Moving the museum whale
description: Move a whale exhibit before the gallery reopens.
image_alt: A large whale exhibit on a wheeled cradle while a surveyor, handler and curator consider the move.
predicament: The survey team knows which passage is usable. The handlers must choose a route. Later, the curator must decide whether the move is complete and the gallery can reopen.
motivation: Change the information arrangements and ask what each person must be able to distinguish to choose their part of the move.
limitation: The museum, layouts and effort units are invented. The checker evaluates the stated information and decision rules.

projects.title: Knowing enough to act together
projects.description: Compare cues, reports and inspections across different local views.

title: Bracken Vale railway
description: Renew a small railway while services keep running.
image_alt: A team discussing a tabletop railway with a junction, station, power upgrade and monitoring project.
predicament: A railway infrastructure team must reconcile passenger and freight needs with access, uncertain condition and limited resources. Junction, station, power and monitoring projects raise different decisions.
motivation: Try practical questions about relationships, planning, evidence, learning and project decisions in one shared fictional setting.
limitation: Every project, figure and relationship is invented. Working examples make the interventions inspectable; human benefit remains to be tested.

projects.title: Small interventions, useful questions
projects.description: Choose a question, change an input and judge what the extra structure adds.
projects.image_alt: A team discussing a tabletop railway with a junction, station, power upgrade and monitoring project.

title: The mountain-festival shuttle
description: Book the buses before the evidence is in.
image_alt: Two small buses wait below festival tents and a mountain trailhead, while an organiser consults a booking sheet.
predicament: A mountain festival needs a shuttle from the village to the trailhead. Reserve one bus or three? Fresh booking counts may help, or a paid demand survey—but the bus-hire hold expires soon.
motivation: Follow what each possible answer lets the organiser decide next. Compare evidence worth buying, evidence that changes nothing, and useful evidence that arrives too late.
limitation: Invented service values support a finite decision model. It compares choices about evidence and commitment; it does not produce an operating timetable or a real transport recommendation.

projects.title: Evidence before commitment
projects.description: When is learning enough to justify paying or waiting before booking?

title: The Island Reading Room
description: Get the books ashore while the jetty is closed.
image_alt: A boat holds boxes of books beside a closed jetty. A shore path leads to a little reading room, with a seal watching from a rock.
predicament: A tiny island reading room needs shelves and books. The books are on the boat; the jetty is unavailable. A low-tide inspection may offer a shore path, but a fixed pallet and hand-carried boxes need different delivery arrangements.
motivation: Follow two coordinators exchanging questions and replies. An answer becomes the other coordinator’s next input; hiding their internal exchange leaves the composed outside interface.
limitation: These are authored routing policies in a finite Geometry of Interaction illustration. The policies do not learn; an inspection report must be supplied from outside. A proposed plan is not a completed or safe delivery.

projects.title: Policies in conversation
projects.description: How does one coordinator’s answer shape the next exchange?
